_comment: Advisories that `npm audit` reports but which are not reachable in this
application. Every entry must carry a justification and an expiry date.
This is NOT a way to defer work on an exploitable finding. An entry is only
legitimate when the vulnerable code path cannot be reached at all. If a fix
exists and is installable, bump the dependency instead.
Entries are checked by .github/scripts/audit-check.mjs. An expired entry is a
hard failure, so every suppression comes back for review on its own.
The ID of an entry goes into `allow-ghsas` of the dependency review in
`workspaces` names the directory an entry was justified for. This repo has
one lockfile, at the root, so it is always ["."].

allow.reason: Among the production dependencies picomatch 4.0.7 comes only through @parcel/watcher, which next-intl uses to watch source files for its message extractor (experimental.extract). The web does not turn the extractor on, so the watcher is never started, and the only patterns it would hand picomatch.makeRe are next-intl's own constant ignore globs. Every other copy comes with a development tool (the Nest CLI, Vite under Vitest, the Next.js ESLint plugin, knip) that matches this repository's own file patterns. None of them ever matches anything a request carries. No fix is installable: the advisory covers every published version up to the latest, 4.0.7. Remove when a patched picomatch is released.
